status: Anima design convention; placement migration remains explicit
principle: Shape reinforces the action promise. Audience, visual prominence and native HTML behavior are separate decisions.

rules.name: Silver tab
rules.meaning: Enter a defined task or workspace.
avoid: Passive navigation dressed as a major task

rules.name: Depth fold
rules.meaning: Advance, review or resolve work already underway.
avoid: Treating it as the creative-audience identity
Using its dark material to imply a less important audience
Claiming Prepare has sent or enrolled anything

rules.name: Liquid capsule
rules.meaning: Offer a personal connection or considered handoff.
avoid: Using the orb to imply a completed match or submission

selectionOrder: State the actual consequence in the label and choose the native link/button/form behavior.
Choose intent: entering a task, working inside it, or seeking a human connection.
Choose prominence independently: featured, peer or supporting. Supporting actions can use the waterline link regardless of their intent.
Apply material and decorative detail deliberately; do not derive appearance from array position or audience category.
composition: One featured capsule per visual region; the orb is a point of attention within one target.
Peer audience choices deserve balanced footprint, label weight, placement and interaction strength. A lighter fill must not accidentally make one audience preferred.
Waterline links handle supporting exploration and utility: Our approach, See an example, Back, Edit, Copy and Download.
A family can be the primary action in its own context. Fold does not mean secondary; silver does not mean business.
No shape is permission to send, publish, delete, pay or contact an agent. Explicit labels and the real review/confirmation flow communicate those consequences.
nativeSemantics: Use a native anchor for a destination and a native button for local actions; form progression/submission retains type=submit.
Keep the orb and arrow decorative inside the same control, not separate focus stops.
Loading, disabled, invalid and completed are states of the same family; retain the label context and expose state explicitly.
The label remains sufficient when gradients, motion or decorative shapes are absent.

roundtable.creativeDirection: Shapes can express threshold, agency and personal invitation, but those metaphors must survive actual user journeys.
roundtable.interactionDesign: Separate action mode, prominence and HTML behavior; index-based or audience-based styling is not a stable contract.
roundtable.accessibleSystem: Labels state consequences; native semantics and one clear target carry behavior. Peer routes must not imply unequal audience importance.
roundtable.disagreement: The fold was proposed both for exploration and for work in progress. The final lead recommendation assigns it to work; supporting exploration already has a waterline link.
roundtable.decision: Threshold → tab; working step → fold; personal invitation → capsule. These are local design conventions, not assumed universal meanings.

migration.current: Approved silver tab / fold trial retained; peer material emphasis refined without geometry changes.
migration.next: Keep the reviewed layout and geometry trial visible. Compare peer entry treatments deliberately; neither audience owns a shape. Explicit metadata now replaces array-index styling.
Use folded working-action treatment in the subsequent placement pass.
